name: Henry Kissinger

summary.text: Henry Kissinger (1923-2023) was U.S. national security adviser (1969-1975) and Secretary of State (1973-1977). This file records only the parts of his public record the site touches: the 1973-75 oil-price documents in the State Department's Foreign Relations of the United States series, including his October 14, 1973 letter to King Faisal on the airlift to Israel, his 1974 memorandum that the Shah's interest in high oil prices ran counter to U.S. interests, and his November 1974 backchannel on the Shah's secret agreement to a price cut; his founding in 1982 of Kissinger Associates, a consulting firm that does not disclose its clients, and his resignation on December 13, 2002 as chairman of the 9/11 Commission rather than disclose them; and his seat on the board of Theranos, profiled by Fortune in June 2014 and retired with the company's board of counselors in 2017. The Iran and Saudi Arabia files hold the FRUS record in full; another file covers the Theranos board.

facts.claim: On October 14, 1973 Secretary of State Kissinger wrote to King Faisal that the United States had no alternative but to begin an airlift of supplies to Israel; a CIA memorandum of October 19 reported that Saudi Arabia had already cut production by 10 percent and that Libya, Abu Dhabi, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia had announced or threatened an embargo against the United States.
facts.quote: Saudi Arabia has reportedly already cut current production by 10%

facts.claim: In a 1974 memorandum recommending a personal letter from President Nixon to the Shah, Kissinger wrote that the Shah's interest in maintaining high oil prices ran counter to the U.S. interest in seeing them lowered.
facts.quote: the Shah's interest in maintaining high oil prices ran counter to the U.S. interest in seeing them lowered

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian (FRUS 1969-76, vol. XXVII)
sources.title: Memorandum from Secretary of State Kissinger to President Nixon

facts.claim: In November 1974, after more than four hours with the Shah in Tehran, Kissinger reported by backchannel to Scowcroft that the Shah would recommend a slight cut in oil prices at the next OPEC meeting, to be held through 1975, which Kissinger estimated at a 20 to 25 percent real reduction over two years, on condition of absolute secrecy.
facts.quote: the Shah made the cut conditional on absolute secrecy

facts.claim: Kissinger was appointed chairman of the 9/11 Commission in November 2002 and resigned on December 13, 2002, after the Senate Ethics Committee advised that commission members must comply with congressional financial-disclosure rules, which would have required him to reveal the clients of Kissinger Associates; in his letter to President Bush he said the disclosures would have forced him to liquidate the firm and that resolving all concerns would have significantly delayed the commission's work.
facts.quote: the detailed financial disclosures required to join the commission would have forced him to liquidate his company, which provides political and security analysis to foreign clients

facts.claim: Fortune's June 2014 profile of the Theranos board listed Kissinger, former Secretary of State and national security adviser, among outside directors that included three former cabinet secretaries, two former senators, a retired admiral and a retired Marine general, most introduced to the company through George Shultz; Fortune argued in October 2015 that the board was assembled for its governmental connections rather than its understanding of the technology.
facts.quote: With three former cabinet secretaries, two former senators, and retired military brass, it's a board like no other.

sources.title: Theranos board directors
Theranos board: a board like no other

facts.claim: Theranos retired its board of counselors, which consisted mostly of former directors with government connections including Kissinger and George Shultz, in 2017.
facts.quote: Theranos is getting rid of high-profile board members including Henry Kissinger and George Shultz

connections.claim: Kissinger founded and ran Kissinger Associates, a New York consulting firm providing political and security analysis to foreign clients, from 1982; its client list is not disclosed, and his unwillingness to disclose it led to his resignation from the 9/11 Commission in December 2002.
connections.quote: his company, which provides political and security analysis to foreign clients
